cases.transcript:

[00:00:13] Let me define a uh term first: debit means an entry that increases assets or expenses Let me define a term first: ledger means the book that collects all accounts.
[00:00:25] Now let us look at the accounting equation. Assets equal liabilities plus equity Every transaction keeps the equation balanced. Now let us look at recording entries.
[00:00:35] Each entry has a debit and a credit of equal value. A trial balance checks that totals match. here is a question to think about before next time. Why must debits always equal credits?

cases.transcript:
[00:00:00] Marcus: Welcome, and thank you for joining me. I am Marcus.
[00:00:04] Kira: Thanks for having me, I am Kira, and I work as an architect.
[00:00:09] Marcus: What would you tell someone just starting out?
[00:00:12] Kira: Write down what you tried, even when it fails. Failed experiments teach you the most.
[00:00:18] Marcus: Why does this work matter to you?
[00:00:21] Kira: Because small errors add up over years. A tiny drift becomes a wrong decision.
[00:00:27] Marcus: What does a normal day look like?
[00:00:30] Kira: I start with the overnight logs, then we review anything that failed. Afternoons are for writing.
[00:00:36] Marcus: I will share the recording once it is edited by Friday.
[00:00:40] Kira: Sounds good, thank you.
[00:00:42] Marcus: I will email you the written questions by Monday.
[00:00:46] Kira: Sounds good, thank you.
[00:00:48] Marcus: Thank you for your time, that was a great conversation.

cases.title: Interview with Ben
cases.transcript:
[00:00:00] Kwame: Welcome, and thank you for joining me. I am Kwame.
[00:00:04] Ben: Thanks for having me, I am Ben, and I work as a pilot.
[00:00:09] Kwame: What role does the community play?
[00:00:11] Ben: Volunteers found most of our bugs. Without them we would still be guessing.
[00:00:16] Kwame: How did the project start?
[00:00:18] Ben: It began when we noticed the sensors drifted every winter. Nobody had measured it before.
[00:00:24] Kwame: What was your biggest early mistake?
[00:00:26] Ben: We trusted the vendor numbers without checking them. Calibration matters more than hardware.
[00:00:31] Kwame: Why does this work matter to you?
[00:00:34] Ben: Because small errors add up over years. A tiny drift becomes a wrong decision.
[00:00:40] Kwame: When will the final report be ready?
[00:00:43] Ben: Good question, I would rather not answer that today.
[00:00:47] Ben: I will share the photos from the field trip.
[00:00:51] Kwame: Sounds good, thank you.
[00:00:53] Kwame: Thank you for your time, that was a great conversation.
